subject: Token slabization, context amortization, and rounding — request for concrete examples
messages:
From: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@aqahealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Mercer <tom.mercer@aqahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: How will billing look for our long-context, repeated-prefix workload?

Hi Rishi,

Quick question as we scope the pilot: our QA assistant sends ~5k calls/day where each call includes a ~20k-token patient context (redacted PHI) plus a ~300-token prompt. We expect high prefix reuse across calls (same patient records reused across short sessions). The procurement team is asking: how does Redwood actually meter and round in this scenario?

Specific asks:
- Are input/context tokens billed each call or amortized when the same prefix is reused?
- Do you round per-call, per-minute, or per-window? What is the billing quantum?
- Any minimums we should plan for on invoices?

Can you send a sample invoice line with numbers for our baseline so we can map to our internal forecast? Also we may need a short note for legal about how prefix caching affects charges.

Thanks — attaching our procurement template.

Regards,
Alice Nguyen
Head of Procurement, AQA Health
[Attachment: procurement_terms.pdf (pdf)]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@aqahealth.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: How will billing look for our long-context, repeated-prefix workload?

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear examples, and great to see the volume detail. Short answer up front: we bill tokens using a combination of a per-call generation quantum and a short-window amortization for repeated prefixes; I'll give concrete numbers and a sample row below.

Key points:
1) Quantum and rounding: generation + returned tokens are rounded up in 512-token blocks for long-context models (this is our default for >32k context variants). Input/context tokens are normally charged at the same unit rate as generation tokens but handled separately in the aggregation rule.

2) Prefix amortization window: when identical prefix content is reused across requests from the same customer within a rolling 45-minute window, we apply a prefix credit: the first call charges full input context tokens; subsequent calls within the window bill the context at 20% of nominal (a 80% credit). The aim is to reflect caching benefits without masking truly distinct contexts.

3) Minimums: invoices will not show micro-charges below our billing floor. For hosted API customers we currently apply a per-call minimum equivalent to 256 tokens (after aggregation) to limit noise from tiny calls; for committed / reserved customers (dedicated), we can set lower per-call floors or waive the floor in contract.

Sample calculation (your baseline: 20k context + 300 prompt, assume 200 tokens returned):
- Call 1 (no prefix cache yet):
  - Input/context tokens: 20,000 -> rounded to blocks: ceil(20000 / 512) * 512 = 40 * 512 = 20,480 billable tokens
  - Prompt tokens: 300 -> rounds to 512 => 512 billable tokens
  - Generation (response): 200 -> rounds to 512 => 512 billable tokens
  - Total billable tokens call 1 = 20,480 + 512 + 512 = 21,504 tokens

- Call 2 (same prefix within 45-min window):
  - Input/context tokens: 20,000 -> prefix credit applies: billed at 20% -> 4,000 -> rounding -> ceil(4000 / 512) * 512 = 8 * 512 = 4,096
  - Prompt tokens: 300 -> 512
  - Generation: 200 -> 512
  - Total billable tokens call 2 = 4,096 + 512 + 512 = 5,120 tokens

So two repeated calls (one cold + one warm) bill ~26,624 tokens total.

If you have bursts where calls are <256 tokens after aggregation, the per-call floor will make the line show 256 tokens for that call unless we contractually waive it.

Attachments: I've added a short worked example sheet (pricing_matrix.xlsx) and a PDF with the same calculations (billing_examples_2026-06.pdf). Vanessa — I copied you in case AQA wants a temporary pilot concession on minimums or a tailored amortization window.

Happy to hop on a quick call to walk this through with procurement/legal.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: pricing_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@aqahealth.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: How will billing look for our long-context, repeated-prefix workload?

Alice — appreciate the clear ask. Two quick commercial notes so your procurement team can budget and legal can see precedent: 

1) Pilot concession: for the 3-month pilot we can (a) reduce the per-call floor to 128 tokens and (b) increase the prefix-credit to bill repeated prefixes at 10% (vs our standard 20%) — this is a short-term concession tied to a 6-month paid committed tier thereafter.

2) Discounting: for the committed annual tier we propose a 15% committed discount on list for the first $350k committed spend, stepping to 20% beyond that tier. We can bake in an override for invoice smoothing on the first billing cycle so their finance team doesn't get surprised by the cold-cache charges.

If that sounds workable, we'll produce amended clause language for the MSLA and an illustrative invoice row. Rishi — please include the revised worked example (I'll review and confirm).

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

On the pilot concession: please confirm whether a 45-minute amortization window is sufficient for clinical workflows or if you'd prefer a per-session (same-patient session) definition instead of a pure time window.

From: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@aqahealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Mercer <tom.mercer@aqahealth.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: How will billing look for our long-context, repeated-prefix workload?

Vanessa / Rishi — thank you. Pilot concession sounds reasonable and helps our cash forecasting. A couple of clarifications from procurement/legal: 
- For the amortization definition we prefer "session-based" semantics instead of a pure rolling clock: bill full context on first call in a session, thereafter apply the credit for calls that reference the same patient session id within the same logical session (session ends after 60 minutes of inactivity). That maps better to our audit logs.
- Please include contract language that the prefix credit only applies to byte-identical prefix content; if customer-side truncation or dynamic metadata causes non-identical prefixes, the credit won't apply.

If you can send a short redline for our procurement template with the floor and prefix credit terms spelled out, we can turn it around from our side next week. Attaching the procurement template again and a quick list of internal POC emails.

Thanks,
Alice
[Attachment: procurement_terms.pdf (pdf)]
